verdict.rationale: GitHub's own docs describe fine-grained personal access tokens. You grant each token a specific set of permissions that define which resources it can reach through the API, which is the scoped credential an agent would use. The REST API also returns an `X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions` header telling you which permissions an endpoint requires, which supports least-privilege tuning. missing for 10: evidence of resource/repository-level scoping and token expiration, an agent-specific identity or credential mechanism (e.g. GitHub Apps or agent tokens), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
